[head=2][color=#e8b04b]Forms of Address[/color][/head]
How you speak to someone says a lot about who you are and where you stand. Each faction in Taypan has its own culture, and using the wrong form of address instantly marks you as an outsider, a fool, or a target. Call an Imperial knight "comrade," or a Union officer "my lord," and everyone in the room will notice. Getting it right is part of good roleplay.
This page is a quick guide. For the ranks and roles behind these titles, see the [color=#e8b04b]Glossary[/color].
[head=3][color=#684871]Divine Sol Mandate (DSM)[/color][/head]
The Mandate's charters and estates are built on rank, privilege, duty, and precedent. Address those above you [bold]formally[/bold], because failing to do so is an insult, and before a noble it may even be a crime.
- A knight, such as a Knight Banneret or Knight Templar, is addressed as [color=#684871][bold]Ser[/bold][/color], as in "Yes, Ser" or "As you command, Ser." - Officers and commanders are called [color=#684871][bold]Sir[/bold][/color] or [color=#684871][bold]Ma'am[/bold][/color]. - Nobles and high lords are called [color=#684871][bold]My Lord[/bold][/color] or [color=#684871][bold]My Lady[/bold][/color], or addressed by an office such as Count or Lord Admiral. - Common soldiers, such as a Man-at-Arms or Freeholder, address each other by name or rank, but they always defer upward.
[head=3][color=#bf4d00]New Crescent Workers' League (NCWL)[/color][/head]
The League is the provisional revolutionary front backed by the Workers' Union. It rejects hereditary titles and treats everyone as a comrade in the struggle, while retaining military and administrative offices.
- Everyone is a [color=#bf4d00][bold]Comrade[/bold][/color], as in "Comrade Kapitan" or "well done, comrade." - Civilians and workers may also be called [color=#bf4d00][bold]Citizen[/bold][/color]. - Officers are addressed by their post rather than any lordship, such as MVD Officer, Unionkapitan, or Flagman. - [color=#d9776c]Never[/color] use "Sir," "My Lord," or noble honorifics. To a Union soldier that language is Imperial rot, and it marks you as an enemy or a bootlicker.
[head=3][color=#535961]Shinohara Heavy Industries (SHI)[/color][/head]
Shinohara is a Japanese megacorporation, and its people speak with polished corporate manners. Rank in the company is rank in the room, so be professional and respectful upward.
- Superiors are addressed by their title, such as Manager or Director, and a respectful [color=#535961][bold]Sir[/bold][/color] or [color=#535961][bold]Ma'am[/bold][/color] is always safe. - Colleagues may add the honorific [color=#535961][bold]-san[/bold][/color] to a name as a sign of respect. - Rudeness toward a superior is treated as a [color=#d9776c]performance issue[/color], because in Shinohara disloyalty is a threat to the company itself.
[head=3][color=#ff7f7f]Taypani Free Companies Federation (TFCF)[/color][/head]
The Federation contains four companies with different internal cultures. Address is usually practical and contractual rather than noble; use a person's company office when it matters.
- The joint leader is the [color=#ff7f7f][bold]Ringleader[/bold][/color]. Company leaders remain the proper authority for internal business. - Crewmates are addressed by name, by nickname, or with a blunt "hey." - Gorlex crews favor direct ranks, Interdyne and Cyberdawn use professional titles, and SAW crews tend toward workplace language. A contract matters more than inherited status.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]General advice[/color][/head]
- When in doubt with a stranger, stay neutral and polite until you know their faction. - Using an [bold]enemy's[/bold] honorifics sincerely can read as mockery or submission, so be aware of what your words signal. - Address is a roleplay tool. Deliberately misusing it, like an Imperial refusing to call a rival lord by title, can be a great way to start tension, as long as you are ready for the consequences.
